newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Exhuming Peron for DNA tests expected this month.
newsitem.headline: Exhuming Peron for DNA tests expected this month.

text.p: The woman who claims she is the daughter of former Argentine populist leader Juan Peron expects his body to be exhumed for DNA tests by the end of the month, her son said on Monday.

Marta Holgado, 62, arrived in Buenos Aires on Sunday to prove that she is the fruit of a secret romance between the general who ruled Argentina from 1946-55 and 1973-74 and her mother in the early 1930s. She says her real name is Lucia Virginia Peron.
Holgado won a court appeal for Peron's remains to be exhumed from a tomb in Buenos Aires' Chacarita cemetery to test his DNA, or genetic material, with her blood samples.

"We believe it should be carried out by the end of the month," her 31-year-old son Horacio told Reuters at the Buenos Aires hotel where she was holed up with lawyers, hoping for a court summons to present additional evidence that she claims includes 20 witnesses to her birthright.

"My mother is quite willing to go to court," said the man who could be proclaimed grandson of Argentina's most famous political leader. Peron died in 1974, but with his second wife Evita, is still evoked by the Peronist Party which is again in power. His body has already been desecrated by thieves who chopped off his hands -- their motive is still unknown.

Holgado, who like her son has a clear resemblance to Peron, says stories about the general being sterile after an accident in 1913 are not true and that Evita and his third wife Isabel, who was president from his death until a military coup in 1967, both aborted children sired by Peron.
"My father received a non-traumatic blow to the testicular zone which didn't bring about any physical damage," she said.
Holgado says her mother was Peron's lover from 1932 during his first marriage, that she first saw him when she was eight, but that she did not learn he was her father until 1953, when she was 19.
She says she was kidnapped and menaced in 1971 by Isabel's henchman Jose Lopez Rega, who also tried to kidnap Horacio and destroyed her birth certificate showing Peron was her father.

Holgado denies she is after any inheritance, reported to include secret Swiss bank accounts. "I am in search of my identity, but if I am declared his daughter, as I am going to be, whatever is mine by law will be welcome," she said.

While some Peronists express indignation at what they see as another threatened profanation of Peron's tomb, the current President Carlos Menem has kept silent. So far, Holgado's face seems her strongest argument. As she told local radio on Monday: "Whenever I look in the mirror, I see Dad."
